column3: title — the course in order; each lesson assumes every one before it.
Being and naming: sein, pronouns, der/die/das
Having things: haben, ein/eine, the accusative
Doing things: regular verbs in the present, the verb second
Saying no: nicht and kein
Asking: W-questions and yes/no questions
Counting: numbers 0–20, prices and age
Verbs that change their vowel: fahren, essen, lesen, sehen…
Family: mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr
More than one: the plural of nouns
Telling the time: the clock, the days, um and am
Dates: the months, im, numbers to 100, der dritte Mai
For me, without you: accusative prepositions and pronouns
Can, must, want: können, müssen, wollen
May, should, would like: dürfen, sollen, möchten; mögen
The day: separable verbs (aufstehen, anrufen, einkaufen…)
Asking and telling: the imperative, bitte
To whom: the dative, helfen, gefallen, gehören
Getting around: mit, nach, bei, von, zu, aus, seit
To me, to you: dative pronouns, es gibt, two objects
What I did: the perfect with haben
Where I went: the perfect with sein; aufgestanden, verstanden
How it was: war and hatte
Where and where to: in, auf, an… with the dative or the accusative
The red dress: adjective endings after der, die, das
A new sofa: adjective endings after ein, kein, mein
Fresh bread, good morning: adjective endings with no article
Bigger, the biggest: comparison, als and wie
Because, that, if: weil, dass, wenn and the verb at the end
I wonder if: indirect questions; als and wenn in the past
So, still, then: deshalb, trotzdem, dann; aber, sondern, denn, oder
Myself: reflexive verbs, sich freuen, sich waschen
Waiting for, thinking of: verbs with prepositions, darauf, worauf
Once upon a time: konnte, musste, wollte; ging, kam, gab, sagte
Would, could: würde, hätte, wäre, könnte
The man who, the film that: relative clauses
Trying to, in order to: the infinitive with zu, um … zu
Whose: the genitive, des Vaters, wegen
What will be: the future with werden; man, jemand, nichts, alle
